name: Buffer
tagline: Schedule your social media posts in bulk across Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn
description: I'll be honest — I tried a few social media schedulers before Buffer, and most of them made me feel stupid. Buffer is the one I actually stuck with. You log in once a week, queue up your posts, and it drip-feeds them throughout the week. No logging in every day, no remembering to post at 2pm. I set it up for a florist client in about 15 minutes and she's been using it ever since. The free plan is genuinely useful, which is rare.

name: Later
tagline: Visual Instagram and TikTok scheduling with drag-and-drop calendar
description: Later lets you visually plan and schedule your Instagram feed, stories, and TikTok content. The drag-and-drop calendar makes it easy to see your entire month at a glance.
pricing: Freemium (Free up to 30 posts, Paid from $25/mo)

name: Calendly
tagline: Automate your appointment booking and eliminate back-and-forth emails
description: Calendly is one of those tools that feels like cheating once you set it up. You send someone a link, they pick a time that works for them, and it automatically goes into your calendar. No more "How about Tuesday?" "No, I'm busy Tuesday, what about Thursday?" emails going back and forth for three days. A coach I know said it saved her about 4 hours a week just on scheduling calls. The free version covers one calendar type which is enough to start.
cons: Complex group events need paid plan

name: Acuity Scheduling
tagline: Client appointment scheduling with payments and intake forms built in
description: Acuity is a powerful scheduling tool designed for service-based businesses. Clients book appointments, sign intake forms, and pay deposits — all in one flow.

name: ManyChat
tagline: Automate Instagram DMs and Facebook Messenger to capture leads while you sleep
description: ManyChat lets you build automated chat flows that respond to comments, DMs, and messages. Set up a keyword trigger and instantly send your lead a booking link or free guide.
pricing: Freemium (Free up to 1,000 contacts, Paid from $15/mo)

name: Mailchimp
tagline: All-in-one email marketing platform with automation for beginners
description: Mailchimp is usually the first place I send people who've never done email marketing before. It holds your hand through the whole process — import your contacts, pick a template, write your email, hit send. The free plan covers up to 500 contacts which is enough for most solo business owners starting out. My main gripe is it gets expensive once your list grows past a couple thousand, but by then you're probably making enough money that the cost doesn't hurt.
pricing: Freemium (Free up to 500 contacts, Paid from $13/mo)

name: ActiveCampaign
tagline: Advanced email automation + built-in CRM for growing small businesses
description: ActiveCampaign combines email marketing with a lightweight CRM. Track leads, automate follow-ups, and build sophisticated funnels that feel personal.

name: HubSpot CRM
tagline: Free CRM that tracks every client interaction and follow-up automatically
description: HubSpot's free CRM is genuinely good — unusual for a free tool from a big company. It tracks every email, call, and meeting with a client automatically. The killer feature for me is the follow-up reminders: you set one and it nags you until you do it. A letting agent I know uses it to track every property viewing and follow-up, and he swears he hasn't lost a lead since. The paid tiers are pricey, but the free version does enough that most small businesses never need to upgrade.

name: Pipedrive
tagline: Visual sales pipeline CRM designed for deal-focused small businesses
description: Pipedrive is built around the sales pipeline. Drag deals through stages, set activity reminders, and know exactly what to do next. Ideal for businesses that live and die by follow-ups.
cons: Can be rigid for non-sales use

name: Canva
tagline: Design professional social media graphics in minutes with drag-and-drop templates
description: I am not a designer. My Instagram posts used to look like a 12-year-old made them in Microsoft Paint. Canva fixed that. You pick a template — for Instagram, Facebook, a flyer, whatever — swap in your own photos and text, and it looks professional. The brand kit thing is useful: you save your colours and fonts once, and every new design automatically uses them. I've seen estate agents and personal trainers put out genuinely good-looking content using nothing but the free version.
cons: Can feel slow on older devices

name: Descript
tagline: Edit video and audio by editing text — then repurpose into clips automatically
description: Descript lets you edit video by editing the transcript. Remove ums, add captions, and turn one long video into 10 short clips with AI. Perfect for content repurposing.

name: Zapier
tagline: Connect your apps and automate repetitive tasks without any code
description: Zapier is the glue that holds everything together. When you get a new enquiry on your website, Zapier can automatically add that person to your email list AND create a contact in your CRM AND send you a Slack notification — all without you lifting a finger. I use it to connect tools that don't normally talk to each other. The free plan gives you 100 tasks per month which is enough for a few basic automations. If you find yourself needing more, the paid plans are reasonable for what you get.

name: Make (Integromat)
tagline: Visual automation builder with more control than Zapier for power users
description: Make offers a visual scenario builder that gives you fine-grained control over your automations. It handles complex logic and large data volumes more affordably than Zapier.

name: Podium
tagline: Automate review requests and manage your local reputation from one inbox
description: Podium helps local businesses collect more reviews automatically. Send review requests via text, manage all conversations in one inbox, and get more 5-star ratings.

name: Birdeye
tagline: All-in-one reputation management with review generation and social listening
description: Birdeye automates the entire review lifecycle. Generate reviews, respond to them from one dashboard, and track your reputation across 200+ directories.

name: FreshBooks
tagline: Automated invoicing and expense tracking designed for solo service businesses
description: FreshBooks makes invoicing painless. Set up recurring invoices, auto-send late payment reminders, and track expenses from your phone. Syncs with your bank for real-time reconciliation.

name: Hootsuite
tagline: Manage all your social media accounts from one dashboard with advanced analytics
description: Hootsuite lets you manage multiple social networks from a single dashboard. Schedule posts, monitor mentions, and get detailed analytics. Best for businesses active on 3+ platforms.

name: Opus Clip
tagline: AI that turns one long video into 10 viral-ready short clips automatically
description: Opus Clip uses AI to analyze your long-form videos and extract the best moments as short clips. It adds captions, finds highlights, and formats them for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.

name: Wave
tagline: Free accounting software with invoicing and receipt scanning for micro-businesses
description: Wave is genuinely free accounting software. Send invoices, scan receipts with your phone, and reconcile bank transactions. Perfect for micro-businesses watching every dollar.

name: ConvertKit
tagline: Email marketing built for creators who want simple automations and tag-based sequences
description: ConvertKit is designed for creators and coaches. Tag-based email sequences let you send the right message to the right person. Visual automations and landing pages make it easy to sell digital products.
pricing: Freemium (Free up to 1k subs, Paid from $29/mo)
